name: Amazon

summary.text: Amazon.com, Inc. is a US-listed (NASDAQ: AMZN) multinational technology and retail company. Its segments include North America and International retail and Amazon Web Services (AWS). In its Q4 2025 results release, Amazon reported net sales of $213.4 billion for the quarter, up 14% year over year, and AWS segment sales of $35.6 billion, up 24%.

facts.claim: Amazon reported Q4 2025 net sales of $213.4 billion, up 14% year over year, with AWS segment sales of $35.6 billion, up 24%.
facts.quote: Net sales increased 14% to $213.4 billion in the fourth quarter, compared with $187.8 billion in fourth quarter 2024. ... AWS segment sales increased 24% year-over-year to $35.6 billion.

facts.claim: Amazon Web Services is reported as a separate segment of Amazon; its Q4 2025 segment sales were $35.6 billion, up 24% year over year.
facts.quote: AWS segment sales increased 24% year-over-year to $35.6 billion.

facts.claim: In July 2021, Luxembourg's National Commission for Data Protection (CNPD) fined Amazon Europe Core S.à r.l. €746 million over its processing of personal data under the EU GDPR; the appeal was dismissed in March 2025 and Amazon appealed further in April 2025.
facts.quote: In July 2021, the Luxembourg National Commission for Data Protection (the “CNPD”) issued a decision against Amazon Europe Core S.à r.l. claiming that Amazon’s processing of personal data did not comply with the EU General Data Protection Regulation. The decision imposes a fine of €746 million and corresponding practice revisions. In March 2025, the Luxembourg Administrative Court dismissed our appeal of the CNPD’s decision.

facts.claim: In December 2021, Italy's Competition Authority (ICA) fined Amazon entities €1.13 billion over marketplace and logistics practices in Italy; the Italian Administrative Tribunal reduced the fine to €752 million in September 2025, and Amazon appealed that ruling in December 2025.
facts.quote: In December 2021, the Italian Competition Authority (the “ICA”) issued a decision against Amazon Services Europe S.à r.l., Amazon Europe Core S.à r.l., Amazon EU S.à r.l., Amazon Italia Services S.r.l., and Amazon Italia Logistica S.r.l. claiming that certain of our marketplace and logistics practices in Italy infringe EU competition rules. The decision imposes remedial actions and a fine of €1.13 billion, which we have paid and will seek to recover pending conclusion of all appeals. In September 2025, the Italian Administrative Tribunal (the “TAR”) affirmed the ICA’s decision but reduced the fine to €752 million.

facts.claim: Since March 2020, private litigants, state Attorneys General and the Federal Trade Commission have filed cases alleging, among other things, price fixing, abuse of dominance and monopolization by Amazon; Amazon says it disputes the allegations.
facts.quote: Since March 2020, private litigants, state Attorneys General, and the Federal Trade Commission have filed cases in the U.S., Canada, and the United Kingdom alleging, among other things: price fixing arrangements between each of Amazon and its vendors and Amazon and its third-party sellers; abuse of dominance, monopolization, and attempted monopolization; and consumer protection and unjust enrichment claims

facts.claim: In April 2024, a jury found that Amazon infringed patents owned by Kove IO and awarded Kove $525 million in damages; Amazon filed a notice of appeal in September 2024.
facts.quote: In April 2024, a jury found that Amazon infringed the asserted patents and awarded Kove $525 million in damages. In August 2024, the court awarded Kove $148 million in pre-judgment interest. In September 2024, we filed a notice of appeal.

facts.claim: Amazon announced on April 20, 2026 that it is investing $5 billion in Anthropic today, with up to an additional $20 billion in the future, building on $8 billion previously invested.
facts.quote: Amazon is investing $5 billion in Anthropic today, with up to an additional $20 billion in the future. This builds on the $8 billion Amazon has previously invested.

facts.claim: Anthropic has committed more than $100 billion over ten years to AWS technologies, and states that it continues to choose AWS as its primary training and cloud provider for mission-critical workloads.
facts.quote: We are committing more than $100 billion over the next ten years to AWS technologies, securing up to 5GW of new capacity to train and run Claude. ... We continue to choose AWS as our primary training and cloud provider for mission-critical workloads.

openQuestions: Site claim (Crash Conduits): 'Amazon's $600M CIA C2S cloud contract' (2013). Not verified. The Nextgov URL I tried returned 404 and web search returned no results. Needs a primary source (CIA/ODNI, GAO, or a contemporaneous major outlet).

Site claim (Transhumanism): French regulator penalty for warehouse surveillance, cut from EUR 32M to EUR 15M in Dec 2025 on appeal. Not verified. The CNIL site search returned no results and the expected CNIL page returned 404. Needs the CNIL deliberation or a Conseil d'Etat ruling.

Site claim (Manufacturing Consent): $14.2M paid to anti-union consultants in 2022, roughly triple the year before. Not verified. The LM-20/LM-21 OLMS filings at the US Department of Labor are the expected primary source (SEC EDGAR was blocked for scripted access).
Amazon's 10-K legal proceedings and any SEC or FTC actions were not retrieved (SEC returned 403 to scripted fetches). Regulatory history is therefore not covered in this draft.

Site entities co-mentioned with Amazon (Microsoft, Nvidia, OpenAI, Google, Andy Jassy, Jeff Bezos, CIA, SoftBank, Lawrence Preston Gise) were not researched as connections. Co-mention alone is not a connection; each needs its own source (for example, Jassy's and Bezos's roles at Amazon, and the Gise/ARPA lineage claim).

Wikipedia notes Amazon's 2024 AWS contract for a top-secret cloud service in Australia (USD 1.3B, with the Australian Signals Directorate). It is not included as a fact because I did not open the cited primary source.
